note: Chapter 3 dialogue, Dry Season (Halvorsen Ranch, Mesquite Wells, the Ocotillo Breaks, the Dry Fork). id, speaker, line, emotion. Speaker voice fields name voice types from voices.json. Original writing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Grass the colour of a paper sack, and the creeks gone to stones. Pell picked his season well.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: That's close enough. Whoever sent you, the answer's what it was last week. Not for four dollars, not for forty.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Nobody sent me, Mrs. Halvorsen. I brought you a paper with your name on it that you never signed.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: My south section, signed over in August. In August I was burying my husband. The only thing I signed was the church register.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The same hand signed for a dead man in Bitter Spring. Who's taking your water?

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Cutter Shale's men pulled the rods out of my north windmill on Sunday. The tank's half mud. I've three hundred head that drink like it's their religion.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Señora! They're back at the north mill, four of them, with a team and a chain to pull the tower down.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Saddle my horse, Teodoro. Mrs. Caddell, you may come and watch me be unreasonable.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll come. I'm told I'm good at unreasonable.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.line: Mrs. Halvorsen. Mr. Shale's compliments. Windmills are dangerous in a high wind. We're taking this one down before it hurts somebody.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: There's no wind, Mr. Kett. There's been no wind since June.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.line: Then it'll be a quiet job. Who's your friend?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Somebody who's read Mr. Shale's paperwork.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's the only one I'll waste. The next goes where I'm looking.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.line: Boys who want to go home, go home. The rest of you, with me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Take the chain off her tower, Mr. Kett. Or don't, and find out what it costs.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.line: Mr. Shale pays me to find out. Take her!

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: My husband built that mill with his own hands and a mail-order catalogue. I'd hate to tell him I let it go for nothing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It won't hold. Not with Cutter sending men every Sunday. What's the next water south?

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: The Ybarra well at Mesquite Wells. Deepest in the county. Rosa Ybarra's people dug it before there was a county. Cutter wants it worse than he wants mine.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: If my cattle are going to live, they walk to that well through the Ocotillo Breaks. One canyon with a bad name, and a woman my age doesn't ride drag anymore.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And you'd like somebody who does.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: I'd like somebody who shoots. I can pay a dollar a head delivered, which is most of what I've got left.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: A dollar a head. I'll count them myself.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Good. I trust a woman who counts. My husband never did, and look where it got him. Married to me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Keep it. When this is over my people will be hungry, and you'll have beef.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: My husband would have liked you. He was terrible with money too.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Go to Mesquite Wells first. Tell Rosa we're coming, and that I'll pay for every bucket. She won't believe the second part. Nobody pays for water.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Water's about to get expensive.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: I'll start gathering. Twenty-four of the strongest, señora? The rest won't walk three days dry.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Twenty-four. Pick the ones with sense, Teodoro. Leave me the old cow with the bell. She and I will wait for rain together.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Adobe and dust and a water tower with a padlock on the ladder. The padlock's new.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: Are you the doctor? Tell me you're the doctor.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'm not. What's happened?

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: Riders. Shale's men, cutting through my yard to water their horses at my well like it was theirs already. My Inés was on the wall. The horse didn't even stop.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: Her leg's broken above the knee. I've set calves. I can't set my own daughter.

lines.speaker: ines
lines.line: Mamá, it doesn't hurt if I don't look at it.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: There's a doctor. There was a doctor. He's at Fausto's cantina, and he has been at Fausto's since spring.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then I'll fetch him.

lines.speaker: fausto
lines.line: If you've come for the doctor, señora, take him. If you've come for his tab, take a chair. It's a long list.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Ah. Another visitor with a face like a summons. I'm afraid I've been struck off, madam. Philadelphia was very firm about it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: There's a girl four doors down with a broken leg. Philadelphia isn't here.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: No. It never is when you need it. Neither are my hands. Look at them. They're having a small earthquake of their own.

lines.speaker: barlow
lines.line: He ain't going nowhere. Doc owes me eleven dollars and a mule's worth of patience. He leaves when I'm paid.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Eleven dollars. Count it, and then go and count something else.

lines.speaker: barlow
lines.line: He's yours, God help you. He snores in Latin.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The doctor's leaving. You can stand aside or lie down. I don't mind which.

lines.speaker: barlow
lines.line: Lady, I skin mules for a living. You're smaller than a mule.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Slower, if you please. The street keeps getting up to meet me.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Why do you care? You don't know the child.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I know the horse.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Mm. A clean break of the femur. She's lucky. Lucky is a word doctors use when they mean something worse was available.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: It wants setting in one pull, and somebody to hold her still. And I'll want a drink. Not for courage. For the shaking.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: One. And then you put the bottle down.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: One. You have my word, which is worth exactly one.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. She deserves your hands, Doctor, not the bottle's.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: You've no idea what you're asking of me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've an idea. Hold them out. Now hold them out steadier.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: There. She'll walk. She'll run, God help her parents.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Set. Not prettily. She'll walk with a hitch, and she'll remember whose hands it was.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: Doctor. You'll eat with us tonight, and you'll sleep in a bed, and nobody in this house will say the word Philadelphia.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Madam, nobody has thanked me in a year. I find I don't know where to put it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You could put it to work. I've people who get shot, and a camp that's short a doctor.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A camp. With outlaws in it, I imagine.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: A drover, a cardsharp, a boy, and a poster of me.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A poster. Well. Then we're both struck off. I'll fetch my bag. It's under Fausto's piano, with my dignity.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: Señora Caddell. Cutter Shale came two days ago with a paper. It says the water under my land belongs to whoever owns the land around it. The syndicate owns the land around it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ingrid Halvorsen's herd is coming to drink from this well. Keep it open for them.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: This well was open before there was a Pell. It'll be open after.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Twenty-four head of the thirstiest cattle in the territory, and I get to ride swing. Hap's going to be sick with envy.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Point is mine. Swing is yours, boy. Drag is for the señora's friend, who eats the dust and gets the blame.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've eaten worse than dust. Push them easy. A thirsty steer runs toward water and away from sense.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: One's broke off! Brindle steer, headed back like he forgot something at home!

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Two ways from here. The Narrows: red walls, one way in and one way out. Or round the mesa: half a day longer and dry the whole way.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Teodoro says the Narrows is where folks get bushwhacked. He says it like he's proud of knowing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The Narrows. Faster's kinder when they're this dry. Keep your eyes on the rim.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Round the mesa. I'd rather lose a day than lose the herd in a rock chute.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Riders on the rim! They're shooting into the herd!

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: They're running, Ruth! They're all running!

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Get to the leaders! Ride up on their flank and turn them, or we lose half the herd in the rocks!

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: Heat lightning. No rain in it, only the noise. Cattle hate the noise.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Teodoro says you sing to them at night so they know where you are. I don't know any songs that ain't rude.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then hum.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Lightning! They're up! They're running!

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: They're milling! You turned them! I seen it done once in Abilene, but that man was a liar.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: We lost some in the rocks. A few will turn up. Most won't.

lines.speaker: dunphy
lines.line: Leave the beeves, lady! Mr. Shale's buying them off you at the price of a bullet!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Billy, stay with the herd. Teodoro, the left side. I'll take the ones who talk.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: There's the tower. Smell it? They smell it.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: Bring them in! The trough's full. Rosa filled it at dawn and dared anybody to say a word.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: How many'd we bring?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: All of them, near enough. Ingrid's going to owe somebody beef.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Not all. Enough to start over on. That'll have to do.

lines.speaker: teodoro
lines.line: The señora will cry. She'll say it's the dust.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Ruth? I rode swing on a real drive. Nobody can ever take that off me now.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. Nobody can.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: We'll bed them down by the dry wash. Billy, first watch. Wake me if they so much as cough.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: If they cough, I'll cough back. That's how it works, ain't it?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ingrid's dollar a head. Twenty-some dollars for three days of dust. Tom would have laughed at me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Six riders on the Bitter Spring road, and one of them sits his horse like he owns the ground under it.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. Eben said you'd be taller. Eben has a romantic notion of widows.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cutter Shale. You were at Harlan's Siding.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: I've been at a great many places. A man in my line gets around. Today I'm at the Ybarra well, with a paper.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: By order of the Territorial Water Board, the waters of this well are adjudicated to the adjoining landholder. The Meridian and Western thanks you for your stewardship.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: My grandfather dug this well with a shovel and a mule. Where was the Water Board?

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Not yet invented, Mr. Ybarra. That's the trouble with the past. It never has the right paperwork.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I've seen forged signatures before. Usually on prescriptions. Yours is better work.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: And you'd be the doctor. Mr. Pell sends his regards. He says you owe Philadelphia an apology.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Get down off the horse, Cutter. We'll discuss your paper on the ground.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Not today. Boys, the lady wants a war. Give her the opening shots.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ride on, Cutter. There are children in this yard, and they're not learning your name today.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Considerate. Eben will be touched. Sundown, Mr. Ybarra. The well is ours at sundown.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: You let him go. He'll be back with more.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He'll be back either way. I'd sooner he came back to a yard with no children's blood in it.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Lanterns on the east road. Four. No, five. Cutter keeps his appointments.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: They're bringing a carcass and coal oil. If they get it down the shaft, the well's poisoned for a year.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then nobody gets near the well. Doc, the roof. Mateo, the shotgun and the door.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: The water's clean. Mateo, the water's clean.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: For tonight. Cutter will come back with more paper, or more men.

lines.speaker: mateo
lines.line: They got it down. A year before it sweetens, if it ever does. My grandfather's well.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then Cutter pays for a year of it.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Mr. Ybarra tells me Cutter keeps a line camp up the Dry Fork. That's where he sleeps when he isn't stealing water.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then that's where he wakes up.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: Señora. Whatever you do up there, my children will hear about it. Do it in a way I can tell them.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I'll ride with you as far as the creek. Somebody should be on hand to dig bullets out of whoever's left.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Another day, Caddell! I'll bring Eben, and Eben will bring the Bible!

lines.speaker: ines
lines.line: Señora Ruth. Are you going to shoot the man with the paper?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go inside, Inés. Help your mother with the lamps.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Line camp's a soddy, a corral and a sentry who's been eating Cutter's beans. Come at it from upwind, if you can manage.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Del, if this goes wrong, you ride for Willow Bend and you don't stop to see how it ended.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: I never stop to see how anything ends. It's why I'm so cheerful.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tom. This is the second name. I thought I'd feel something by now besides tired.

lines.speaker: sentry
lines.line: Somebody's in the brush! Cutter! Cutter, she's here!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cutter Shale. Come out with your hands empty. I'd hate to make a liar of your brother's Bible.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Caddell! You came all this way to die in a dirt house? Eben will write you a hymn!

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Enough! Enough, I'm done. You want me in a cell? Pell will have me out by Sunday dinner.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Harlan's Siding, Cutter. Tom Caddell, in the door of the express car. Who fired?

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Eben. Eben always fires first. It's how he says grace. I held the car door, Asa held the horses, Arliss counted the money. Now you know. Doesn't help, does it?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Get up. You're going to Bitter Spring, and you're going to say that again in front of a sheriff.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Mabry? Mabry owes his badge to us. You're delivering me to my own front porch.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then we'll knock very loudly.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. I've seen what Pell's paper does to a cell door.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: That's one. I hope it was worth what it cost you, Ruth. I truly do.

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: My boys know this road better than you, Caddell. Every bend of it.

lines.speaker: dunphy
lines.line: Cut him loose and you can ride away! Nobody needs to die over Cutter!

lines.speaker: cutter
lines.line: Speak for yourself, Harl.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: Cutter Shale. In my jail. On a widow's word.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: On his own word. Ask him who held the car door.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: I know who held the door, Mrs. Caddell. Everybody in this county knows. Knowing has never been the trouble.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: I'll hold him. I'll hold him for the circuit judge, and the judge will be one of Pell's, but by God I'll hold him.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Riders on the ridge! Cutter's whole crew heard the shot. Ride, Ruth!

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Del says it's done. One of them. You don't look any lighter for it.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: In Mabry's jail! Now there's a sentence I never thought to hear in English.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I've buried patients I liked better. I've rarely buried one who deserved it more. I find that doesn't help.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A trial. How quaint. Pell will hate it. Lawyers despise a court they didn't buy first.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Did he say anything? At the end?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Nothing you need, Billy.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: You brought him in alive. I'd have shot him. I'd have wanted to.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Wanting's free. The rest costs.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cutter's done, Tom. Eben and the boy are left. I thought this part would feel like something.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Smell that? Rain. First in four months. Ingrid's cattle will think it's the Second Coming.
